title: 36th Infantry Division 100th Anniversary (Long Version)
description: Actor Gary Sinise provides the introduction for the 36th Infantry Division, Texas Army National Guard as the division celebrates its 100th Anniversary on July 18th, 2017.  The video follows the division through the original muster at Camp Bowie, Texas, and into World War I, World War II, the Texas Army National Guard transformation through the years, the Global War on Terrorism, Defense Support to Civil Authorities and training exercises at home and abroad.  Written approval for music use has been received from the artists and recording companies.

transcript.text: ^- Congratulations to the 36th Infantry Division
^on 100 years of honorable service to our nation.
During World War One, you fought valiantly
across France and then returned to the European continent
in 1943 as you stormed the Italian beaches
near Siciliano, during World War Two.
You liberated Rome and then went on
to fight in both Germany and France.
When our homeland was attacked on September 11th 2001,
you answered the call to fight the global war on
terror in both Iraq and Afghanistan.
We've also helped bring peace and stability
to troubled regions like the Balkans,
Central America and the Sinai Peninsula
of Egypt among many others.
Across Texas, you stand ready to battle floods,
wildfires, hurricanes and whatever else may come.
As others are fleeing the storm, you're on your way in.
You're both active and reserve component soldiers
in your ranks, so many of you stand ready
for any military mission, while
also maintaining civilian careers.
Since the birth of our nation,
citizen soldiers like you have answered the call
to keep us free and secure and we can't thank you enough.
To those Arrow Head soldiers currently deployed,
stay safe over there and come home soon.
To your families, I truly appreciate
all you do to keep the home fires burning
while your soldiers are gone.
You are the unsung heroes, we have a grateful nation.
I'm proud of all the 36th has done over the last
100 years, both at home and overseas, in spite of hell.
^(patriotic marching band music)
(intense music)
^(somber music)
^- [Announcer] That is the World Trade Center
^and we have unconfirmed reports this morning,
^that a plane has crashed into one of the towers.
(panicked screaming)
- [Woman] Oh my god, another plane as just hit.
^- [Presenter] Thousands of people
^that have been running from inside these buildings
^and they said there was just pandemonium.
- I can hear you, the rest of the world hears you
and the people who've knocked these buildings down,
will hear all of us soon.
(intense music)
(somber music)
(dramatic music)
(inspiring music)
